{
  "frontend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Implementation instructions for frontend clients (scope decided from requirement):

Goal (exact contract): For item GET, PUT, DELETE requests only, handle the two new error response shapes exactly as below from the backend and map them to 404 and 403 error flows respectively. Do not change how authentication (401/403 auth flows if currently different) and 422 validation errors are parsed and handled — those must remain using the current frontend parsing logic. Do not assume the new structure applies to any other endpoints or status codes.

Exact backend error bodies to expect for affected cases:
- 404 Not Found (resource missing for item GET/PUT/DELETE):
  HTTP/1.1 404
  Content-Type: application/json
  Body: {"error":{"code":"ITEM_NOT_FOUND","message":"Item not found"}}

- 403 Forbidden (permissions insufficient for item GET/PUT/DELETE):
  HTTP/1.1 403
  Content-Type: application/json
  Body: {"error":{"code":"ITEM_FORBIDDEN","message":"Not enough permissions"}}

Frontend implementation steps:
1. Narrow scope: apply changes only to code paths that call the API endpoints that GET, PUT or DELETE an "item" resource (controllers/actions/services that perform these item requests). Do not alter global/error-parsing utilities used by all endpoints unless they can be made conditional by endpoint/route.

2. Response handling order (must be explicit):
   a. First inspect HTTP status code of the response.
   b. If status is 404 or 403 AND the request was for an item GET/PUT/DELETE, attempt to parse response body as JSON and read response.error.code.
      - If response.error.code === "ITEM_NOT_FOUND" (for 404) or === "ITEM_FORBIDDEN" (for 403), map to the frontend’s item-not-found and item-forbidden flows (UI message, navigation, retry logic, etc.). Use the message field for display if desired.
      - If the body is not valid JSON or does not contain error.code, fall back to the existing error handling for that status (do not crash).
   c. Else for other status codes (including 401, 422, 500, other 4xx/5xx): continue using the current parsing and error flows already implemented in the app (do not force these to conform to the new error object shape).

3. Parsing resilience and feature flagging:
   - Do not assume every 403/404 will include the new error structure; code must tolerate missing/changed body and fallback to existing behavior.
   - Do not attempt to parse every error response as the new structure globally. Limit parsing to item endpoints or branch by status + endpoint context.

4. Unit/integration tests to add/update:
   - Test: item GET when backend returns 404 with exact new body -> frontend must take the item-not-found path and show message matching message field.
   - Test: item PUT/DELETE when backend returns 403 with exact new body -> frontend must take the item-forbidden path.
   - Test: item request returns 404 with a different body or invalid JSON -> frontend must fall back to existing error handling and not throw.
   - Test: non-item endpoints that return 404/403 should not be parsed as the new structure (existing behavior unchanged).
   - Test: authentication error (401) and 422 validation error -> existing parsing and UI behavior unchanged.

5. Logging and metrics: record when the client receives an ITEM_NOT_FOUND or ITEM_FORBIDDEN code (optional) but do not change production telemetry semantics unless explicitly required.

6. Backwards compatibility: do not implement aggressive normalization that rewrites or forces other errors into this shape. Maintain existing behavior for other error classes.

Acceptance criteria (frontend):
- For item GET/PUT/DELETE, when backend responds with the exact new JSON and status (404/403), the frontend uses the corresponding item-not-found / item-forbidden flow.
- For authentication (401) and 422 validation errors, frontend behavior remains the same as before.
- Tests exist and pass for the cases above.

Do not change any backend expectations or invent additional response shapes — follow the exact JSON bodies and status codes above."
  },
  "backend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Implementation instructions for backend servers/services (scope decided from requirement):

Goal (exact contract): For item resource operations (only GET, PUT, DELETE on the item resource), return these exact JSON error bodies for the two cases below with their respective status codes. Do not include a top-level "detail" field. Do not change the structure of authentication errors or 422 validation errors; leave them unchanged.

Exact responses required for item GET/PUT/DELETE when these conditions occur:
- Item not found -> status 404 and body:
  {"error":{"code":"ITEM_NOT_FOUND","message":"Item not found"}}

- Insufficient permissions -> status 403 and body:
  {"error":{"code":"ITEM_FORBIDDEN","message":"Not enough permissions"}}

Implementation steps:
1. Scope: apply this change only to request handlers/controllers/middleware that serve item GET, PUT, DELETE operations. Do not modify other endpoints or global error formats used by unrelated resources unless you can conditionally apply the change only for item endpoints.

2. Where to change:
   - If there is centralized error-handling middleware that returns JSON for all endpoints, modify it only if you can detect the request was for an item GET/PUT/DELETE and then return the new shapes. Otherwise, return these objects directly from the item controllers/service layer when detecting not-found or forbidden conditions.

3. Serialization and headers:
   - Ensure Content-Type: application/json in the response.
   - Response bodies must be exactly the JSON objects above (no extra top-level fields such as "detail", no additional wrapper fields). The order of object keys is not significant, but structure must match.

4. Preserve existing auth and validation error formats:
   - Do not change the shape or status codes for authentication errors (e.g., 401 Unauthorized or any existing auth-related 403 that is not the item-forbidden case) or for 422 validation errors. Those must keep their original structures and codes.

5. Behavior details and edge cases:
   - If an item GET/PUT/DELETE triggers both a validation/auth and a not-found/forbidden condition, follow the existing precedence rules in your codebase. Do not invent new precedence; if not defined, do not change existing behavior.
   - If internal server errors (5xx) occur, do not convert them to the new shapes.

6. Tests to add/update:
   - Unit/integration tests for item GET/PUT/DELETE that assert:
     a) When resource does not exist, response is HTTP 404 with exact JSON {"error":{"code":"ITEM_NOT_FOUND","message":"Item not found"}}.
     b) When caller lacks permission, response is HTTP 403 with exact JSON {"error":{"code":"ITEM_FORBIDDEN","message":"Not enough permissions"}}.
     c) Authentication failure (e.g., missing/invalid token) responses remain unchanged (assert existing shape and status).
     d) 422 validation errors remain unchanged.
   - Tests should also assert Content-Type: application/json for the two new responses.

7. Deployment notes:
   - Deploy this change only when frontend has been updated to branch by status and error.code as specified. If frontend compatibility is a concern, coordinate rollout; do not invent fallback behavior here.

Acceptance criteria (backend):
- Item GET/PUT/DELETE endpoints return the exact JSON bodies and status codes described when the item is missing or permissions are insufficient.
- Authentication errors and 422 validation errors remain unchanged.
- Automated tests verifying these behaviors exist and pass.

Do not change any other error contracts or invent additional response shapes beyond the two exact objects and codes specified above."
  }
}
